reason: the performance lens's findings only the code can fix

findings.text: performance lens, low: plugin.sh runs a `$(cd ...)` subshell at load time to locate claim.sh, a fork the design decision document explicitly said to avoid by not having plugin.sh source claim.sh at all. (plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh: "_ccgl_plugin_dir="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)""; happens when: Every time plugin.sh is loaded for the first time in a process (guarded by `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_GH_LABELS_LOADED`, so once per runner process). The design doc for this issue states: 'plugin.sh must not source core/claim/claim.sh — that would create a circular dependency and add a startup $(cd ...) subshell in plugin.sh's load path.' The code does exactly what the design said not to do.; fix: code)

performance lens, low: `_ccgl_read_holder` calls `$(_ccgl_backend)` — a subshell that only echoes a variable — while the other new functions in claim.sh (`_zbuild_claim_read_labels_into`, `_zbuild_claim_add_label_direct`) explicitly replaced the same pattern with `${ZBUILD_CLAIM_BACKEND:-gh}` to avoid the fork. (core/claim/claim.sh: "case "$(_ccgl_backend)" in"; happens when: When `zbuild:claimed` is already on the issue and `zbuild_claim_acquire` calls `_ccgl_read_holder` on the conflict path; not in a hot loop, but the inconsistency is introduced here while the design comments in the same file call it out as avoided elsewhere.; fix: code)
